subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Should OpenClaw add a synchronous plugin/runtime config pre-apply veto API, and what ordering, metadata, and failure semantics should it use?
rationale: The issue asks for a new plugin API that can block security-sensitive config writes; repository policy treats plugin APIs, config mutation, auth/provider state, startup behavior, and fallback semantics as compatibility-sensitive maintainer choices.

options.title: Design the veto API in the RFC
options.body: Keep this open and resolve hook shape, actor metadata, SecretRef/preflight ordering, fail-closed behavior, recursion rules, and shared-helper coverage through the config validation/mutation RFC before implementation.

options.title: Limit to core validation only
options.body: Decline the plugin veto API and continue strengthening built-in validation, SecretRef preflight, allowlists, and doctor repair paths while accepting that external validators cannot be mandatory.

options.title: Keep validators as optional packages
options.body: Ask contributors to keep config guards as skills/plugins without a core pre-apply seam, which preserves core size but does not solve the bypass described here.

recommendation.title: Design the veto API in the RFC
recommendation.body: Keep this open and resolve hook shape, actor metadata, SecretRef/preflight ordering, fail-closed behavior, recursion rules, and shared-helper coverage through the config validation/mutation RFC before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already provided the explicit product-routing review tying this item to the config validation/mutation RFC direction.
